narration_v2.01: That morning in Qatar, my microscope was sitting on the desk. The photograph was posted in July 2017.
narration_v2.02: I had bought the microscope near Qasr El Einy in Cairo. Bringing it back to Qatar was a considerable hassle.
narration_v2.03: Once it was home, I could return to an observation whenever a question interested me. I wanted that freedom.
narration_v2.04: University laboratories offered more sophisticated instruments and formal protocols. My own microscope served a different, personal purpose.
narration_v2.05: This was a vacation morning, with books and notes beside the microscope. It was not an assigned experiment.
narration_v2.06: I could look again, change the angle, and take another day to think about what I had seen.
narration_v2.07: The instrument could enlarge an object. But a persuasive explanation would still need controls and careful documentation.
narration_v2.08: The microscope lived among ordinary things on my desk. I used it to follow questions outside scheduled laboratory work.
narration_v2.09: I carried it from Cairo to Qatar. Years later, I still remember what having an instrument at home made possible.
